C1.quote: con tapp quise explorar la idea de que las clases implican predicados y que el codigo es dato.
C1.statement: A type is a proposition and belonging to a type asserts a guarantee about the value, so types (including function types) are defined by the invariants, preconditions and postconditions they must satisfy.

C10.quote: que tenga los mínimos componentes nativos posibles, cosa que básicamente sea así, un lenguaje puente
C10.statement: Luthier is language-agnostic: it describes and verifies concepts and equivalences while delegating execution to external code (extern), orchestrating other languages as a kind of butler, with the external world modeled as its own kind of element.

C2.quote: La idea central del tapp es que al declarar una funcion vos declaras que es lo que la funcion debe cumplir como un test y entonces es posible generar tests automaticos.
C2.statement: Defining a function also defines the test over it, and that test is run either exhaustively/deductively when provable or statistically (Bayesian sampling) when not, yielding a probability of success rather than a binary certification.

C3.quote: no la semilla ni los rangos del generador, así que la corrida no es reproducible desde el certificado. Lo arreglo: cada corrida elige y guarda una semilla, guarda los parámetros de generación y una descripción del dominio de cada variable
C3.statement: A certificate is evidence tied by hash to the code and interpreter, graded by level (proved, exhaustive, sampled with named generators and statistical level), and it records the generators, seed and parameters so it is reproducible and composable.

C4.quote: tendría que ser que solamente hay tipos y hay funciones
C4.statement: Luthier has a tiny core (types and functions, with Pi, Sigma, sum, data, subtype, holes) from which everything else is built, self-extensible and executable by hand with pencil and paper like Lisp.

C5.quote: tiene una función, esta función puede ser implementada de muchas maneras, son los distintos paths y cada forma tiene una precisión y una velocidad
C5.statement: A function has many implementations (paths), each with its own precision, speed, memory and place of execution; Luthier is at once declarative and an optimization tool that declares what is wanted and openly compares equivalent paths.

C6.quote: Hay que pensar que el código de Luthier sea un elemento de Luthier ya también desde el vamos. El código es el primer elemento.
C6.statement: Code is data: a Luthier program is itself an element of Luthier (meta-recursion is native from the start), modeled as a DAG of definitions where statements commute and temporality emerges from dependency.

C7.quote: el **hueco**: una definición con tipo y sin cuerpo, `f : A → B := ?`. Una sola cosa cumple cinco papeles: axioma, input del programa, función externa que el entorno llena, definición pendiente, código muerto. Tu principio "no ejecutás hasta que está definido" es su semántica exacta
C7.statement: A hole is a declaration without a body, a first-class citizen that plays at once the role of axiom, program input, external function, pending definition and dead code; nothing is executed until it is defined.

C8.quote: de qué función de olvido le aplicás a los tipos, es un, digamos, eso te define básicamente el lenguaje que estás hablando ... los functores de olvido serían, digamos, uno de los componentes más importantes de Luthier
C8.statement: The forgetful functor is a central mechanism: a value carries the history of operations applied to it, and a non-invertible selective-forgetting map keeps the decoration from outgrowing the value; which forgetting function you apply defines the language you speak.

C9.quote: muchas funciones y tipos van en conjunto ... como los objetos matemáticos, como el grupo ... si vos tenés un objeto matemático, está definido todo junto. O sea, vos no podés definir una parte sola del objeto matemático
C9.statement: Many functions and types form a single mathematical object defined whole by coupled, genuinely dependent laws (its definition graph is a connected cycle); a law relating several functions belongs to the group, not to any one function.
